manifest.name: Payment Provider: Flutterwave
manifest.summary: A Nigerian payment provider covering several African countries.

relations: no new fields; 9 methods overriding payment's reference/rendering/request/notification hooks
flutterwave_customer_email (Char, email tied to the saved Flutterwave card token)

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on base.group_system field groups guarding flutterwave_secret_key / flutterwave_webhook_secret.

views.note: No own model views; xml_loc=47 is view inheritance (payment.provider form: Flutterwave public/secret/webhook keys) plus QWeb: a redirect_form template (POST self-submitting form to the Flutterwave hosted payment link) and an authorization redirect_form (redirect_form_view_id, used by _get_specific_processing_values to bounce the payer to the 3-D Secure auth_url), plus payment_provider_data.xml.

behavioral_notes.observation: The outbound acquirer call (gap #7) is centralized through payment's payment.provider._send_api_request, which payment_flutterwave targets at https://api.flutterwave.com/v3/ via _build_request_url and authenticates with 'Authorization: Bearer <flutterwave_secret_key>' (_build_request_headers; secret stored on the provider, group_system-guarded). _get_specific_rendering_values (redirect/hosted-checkout flow) POSTs to 'payments' a payload of tx_ref(=self.reference), amount, currency, redirect_url(=/payment/flutterwave/return), customer{email,name,phonenumber}, customizations{title=company,logo} and payment_options (const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING), then embeds the returned data['link'] as the api_url of a self-submitting redirect form -- the payer is sent off-site to Flutterwave's hosted checkout. _send_payment_request (saved-token / online_token charge) POSTs to 'tokenized-charges' with token(=token_id.provider_ref), email(=token_id.flutterwave_customer_email), amount, currency, country, tx_ref, first/last name, customer ip and an auth redirect_url(=/payment/flutterwave/auth_return), then folds the response into _process('flutterwave', ...). _parse_response_content returns response.json()['data']; _parse_response_error returns json['message']. None of this server-to-server HTTP is visible in Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_processing_values -> 3-D Secure authorization redirect for pending token charges
behavioral_notes.observation: After a tokenized charge, if _flutterwave_is_authorization_pending() matches (provider_code=flutterwave, operation=online_token, state=pending, provider_reference ilike 'https'), _apply_updates has stashed the bank's 3-D Secure authorization URL into provider_reference (meta.authorization.redirect from the charge response). _get_specific_processing_values then renders provider_id.redirect_form_view_id with {auth_url: provider_reference} to bounce the payer to the issuer's 3DS page; on success Flutterwave returns to /payment/flutterwave/auth_return. The provider_reference is later overwritten with the real Flutterwave transaction id once the tx leaves pending. This stateful overloading of provider_reference (URL while pending, transaction id afterwards) is pure runtime behavior invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: FlutterwaveController return / auth_return / webhook routes -> verify-by-reference + verif-hash signature + state mapping
behavioral_notes.observation: Three public routes settle the transaction. /payment/flutterwave/return (GET) handles the browser redirect from hosted checkout: unless status=='cancelled' it calls _verify_and_process(data), which locates the tx via payment.transaction._search_by_reference('flutterwave', data) and then makes a server-side GET 'transactions/verify_by_reference' (params tx_ref=tx.reference) to re-fetch the authoritative result from Flutterwave before _process('flutterwave', verified_data) -- never trusting the redirect payload. /payment/flutterwave/auth_return (GET) parses the stringified JSON 'response' arg and delegates to the same return handler. /payment/flutterwave/webhook (POST, csrf=False) handles event=='charge.completed': it _search_by_reference, and IF a tx is found, verifies the inbound 'verif-hash' header against provider.flutterwave_webhook_secret with hmac.compare_digest (constant-time; missing/mismatched -> werkzeug Forbidden 403) before tx_sudo._process(...). Status mapping (_apply_updates) folds Flutterwave statuses into payment's state machine via const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING: pending/'pending auth'->_set_pending, successful->_set_done, cancelled->_set_canceled, failed->_set_error, unknown->_set_error+warning. Signature trust, the verify-by-reference round-trip, and the inbound state transitions are all invisible to metadata.

Override of payment's _compute_reference singularizes the prefix with the current datetime (payment_utils.singularize_reference_prefix) because Flutterwave requires the tx_ref to be unique per merchant account; if no prefix is supplied it manually calls _compute_reference_prefix first so the reference is still named after the source document. This shapes the cross-system key (Odoo reference == Flutterwave tx_ref) and is not derivable from field metadata.

When the charge response carries card.token, _extract_token_values vaults a payment.token: provider_ref = card.token, payment_details = card.last_4digits, flutterwave_customer_email = customer.email. Subsequent off-session charges (_send_payment_request) read token_id.provider_ref + token_id.flutterwave_customer_email to POST tokenized-charges. The token lifecycle and the email-tied vaulting are runtime side-effects beyond metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; one outbound endpoint -- https://api.flutterwave.com/v3/ (direct REST, Bearer secret-key auth) -- declared/used in models/payment_provider.py (_build_request_url/_build_request_headers). No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_flutterwave configures via the _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_content / _parse_response_error hook overrides. There is no client-side acquirer SDK: payment is collected via Flutterwave's HOSTED checkout page (server returns a payment link the browser is redirected to), so the only external channel is server-to-server REST plus the redirect/webhook return loop. This is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata.

/payment/flutterwave/auth_return (3-D Secure authorization return -> delegates to the return handler)

external_integrations.sdk: none (hosted-checkout redirect model); server side uses no python SDK -- HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
external_integrations.auth: Bearer <flutterwave_secret_key> (direct REST API); inbound webhook authenticated by a 'verif-hash' header compared against flutterwave_webhook_secret
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.flutterwave.com/v3 (payments / tokenized-charges / transactions/verify_by_reference) authenticated with a secret API key; payment collected via Flutterwave's HOSTED checkout page (the browser is redirected to a Flutterwave-hosted link, optionally through an issuer 3-D Secure page); inbound settlement via a verif-hash-verified webhook plus a redirect-return route that re-verifies the result server-side. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Flutterwave endpoints, the Bearer-key auth, the verif-hash webhook trust, or the verify-by-reference round-trip are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading models/payment_provider.py + models/payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

African / multi-currency acceptance (card, M-Pesa, bank transfer, Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover across const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES)
3-D Secure authentication (redirect to the issuer authorization page)
Tokenization / Saved Cards (vault Flutterwave card token + customer email; off-session tokenized-charges)
Server-side result verification (transactions/verify_by_reference) before confirming state
value_streams: Collect-Payment (Flutterwave): initiate tx -> POST payments (api.flutterwave.com) -> redirect to Flutterwave hosted checkout (optional 3DS) -> redirect /payment/flutterwave/return OR async /payment/flutterwave/webhook (verif-hash) -> verify_by_reference -> _process -> state machine done/error -> downstream post-process settlement

Tokenize-and-Recharge: successful charge + card.token -> vault payment.token (token + email) -> later off-session POST tokenized-charges (online_token), with 3DS auth_return bounce if the issuer requires it
Authorize-3DS: tokenized charge returns pending + auth URL -> _get_specific_processing_values redirects payer to issuer 3DS page -> /payment/flutterwave/auth_return -> verify -> _process

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_flutterwave is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the cardholder/mobile-money payer and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Flutterwave's African card & mobile-money network. It exhibits the three mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (API-key/webhook-secret management, currency & payment-method enablement, exclusion from validation flows), service provisioning (creating the hosted payment link / tokenized charge per transaction and re-verifying the result), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.flutterwave.com link, the hosted-checkout redirect, and the verif-hash-verified settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Flutterwave realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe.metamodel.json (network/support) and the parent payment.metamodel.json (network/support).

typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card or mobile-money payments through Flutterwave in a supported African market
save-card-for-later and tokenized recurring charges (online_token tokenized-charges)

common_gaps: no manual capture / authorize-only / void: Flutterwave here is a direct charge + (full) refund acquirer; partial/manual capture is not implemented
hosted-checkout redirect only -- no inline (PCI-light) client-side card Element; the payer always leaves the site to Flutterwave
the public-URL requirement for webhooks means local/dev instances need a tunnel; the redirect-return + verify_by_reference path is the primary settlement guarantee
currency support is bounded by const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (a static list last refreshed Nov 2022); newer currencies/methods need code changes
no Connect-style merchant self-onboarding: API keys are entered manually on the provider form
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
